title: Multi-region orchestration data model and CRUD checklist (working notes)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working note capturing a compact data model and pragmatic CRUD API checklist for the control plane entities we need to support multi-region orchestration and routing policies. Goal: converge on thin canonical entities, clear ownership, and operational semantics (idempotency, validation, rollout) so downstream routing, billing, and runtime components can depend on stable contracts.

Background & constraints (short):
- Customers may pin resources (models, deployments) to: environment (prod/staging), region(s), and clusters (GPU pools).
- Requests must be routable by policy (latency, cost, compliance) with automatic fallbacks.
- Control plane is separate from per-customer private control planes; this doc focuses on central registry semantics used by hosted and dedicated flows.
- Must support fast read paths for routing (low-latency metadata lookups) and eventual consistent state for slow operations (provisioning, migrations).

Key entities (canonical):
- Resource: unique platform object representing something we serve (model-version, endpoint, dataset slice). Fields: resource_id (UUID), resource_type (model|endpoint|embedding-index), owner_team, pinned_version, default_region_set, created_by, created_ts, tags.
- Environment: logical environment (dev|staging|prod) with policy defaults and quota buckets. Fields: env_id (short), sla_profile, allowed_regions[], billing_meter_id.
- Region: cloud region identifier and capabilities (e.g., g4dn, a100). Fields: region_id (e.g., us-west1), capabilities[], region_cost_multiplier, geo_compliance_tags.
- Cluster: a physical/virtual pool within a region. Fields: cluster_id, region_id, hardware_profile, capacity_units, alloc_policy (shared|dedicated|ephemeral), health_state, labels.
- Binding: a first-class relation that ties Resource + Environment + Region(s) + optional Cluster preference. Fields: binding_id, resource_id, env_id, region_preferences (ordered), cluster_constraints, status (active|draining|migrating).
- RoutePolicy: policy defs used by the router. Types: primary-preference, latency-first, cost-first, geo-fence, compliance-only. Fields: policy_id, policy_type, selectors, failover_order, ttl_cache_seconds.

Design notes (rationale):
- Keep Binding object to drive routing decisions rather than embedding region lists into Resource. That lets us have multiple bindings (same resource, different envs or SLAs).
- Store small denormalized copies of cluster capabilities inside the Binding for fast router decisions (e.g., supports-quantized-int8: true). Denormalize, but authoritative source remains Cluster record.
- Routing decisions must be doable from a single read from a fast metadata store (Dynamo/Spanner/Redis layer): routing key => binding + small cluster snapshot. Longer-running operations consult canonical DB.

CRUD API checklist (behavioral contract)
General rules across endpoints:
- All writes are authored by control-plane services with an idempotency-key header accepted.
- Validation is strict for CREATE but lenient for UPDATE (allow partial patches).
- Every write emits an event to the event bus (resource.created/updated/deleted; binding.status_changed).
- Soft-delete semantics with tombstones for 90 days.

Representative endpoints (REST-shaped for clarity):
1) Resources
- POST /v1/resources  -> create resource. Body includes resource_type, owner_team, pinned_version (optional), default_region_set. Returns 201 + resource_id. Validation: owner_team must exist.
- GET /v1/resources/{resource_id} -> canonical record. Returns denormalized bindings summary.
- PATCH /v1/resources/{resource_id} -> partial update (owner transfer, tags). PATCH must reject changes to resource_type.
- DELETE /v1/resources/{resource_id} -> soft-delete, initiates cascade: scheduler stops new allocations, sets bindings to draining.

2) Bindings (routing anchor)
- POST /v1/bindings -> create binding. Required: resource_id, env_id, region_preferences (ordered list), cluster_constraints (optional), ttl_cache_seconds (suggest). Returns binding_id.
- GET /v1/bindings/{binding_id} -> full binding record + last_provision_ts.
- PATCH /v1/bindings/{binding_id} -> change region_preferences, set status (draining,migrating,active). PATCH triggers a validation run against Cluster capabilities.
- DELETE /v1/bindings/{binding_id} -> mark draining then delete when no active connections.

3) Clusters & Regions (ops-facing)
- POST/PUT for cluster lifecycle (/v1/clusters). Cluster registration is authenticated for infra/ops only.
- GET /v1/clusters?region=us-west1&capability=int8 -> list matching nodes for scheduler use.

4) RoutePolicy (authoring by platform/product)
- POST /v1/route_policies -> create policy. Policy selectors are label-matchers (resource tags, env id).
- GET /v1/route_policies/{id} -> resolve to concrete binding order given current state.

Operational semantics and corner cases:
- Idempotency: clients must pass Idempotency-Key. Server stores idempotency map (operation key -> outcome) for 24 hours.
- Conflict resolution: PATCH with precondition header If-Match: <etag> or optimistic version field. For long ops (provisioning) we use operation objects that can be polled.
- Fast reads: implement a read cache that materializes (binding_id -> ranked cluster candidates) updated by change events. Router should query this cache, not primary DB.
- Rollout strategy for binding changes: 1) PREPARE (validate), 2) SCHEDULE (dry-run), 3) ACTIVATE (switch traffic), 4) MONITOR (health), 5) COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Each stage writes status transitions.

Routing policy examples (behaviors):
- latency-first: prefer clusters with lowest p50 latency for the model footprint; fallback to second region if p95 exceeds threshold.
- cost-first: prefer cheaper region/clusters if expected token-cost > threshold. Also respects geo_compliance_tags.
- geo-fence: only route to regions with allowed geo tag; on violation, route to dedicated fallback (synchronously fail if no allowed regions).
- canary-rollout: route small percentage to new binding cluster; automatic rollback on quality regression.

Security, ownership, audit:
- Every write requires platform RBAC. owner_team on Resource is authoritative for business-level decisions; ops-team owns Cluster records.
- Audit logs (who changed binding/when) kept in write-ahead event stream and linked in resource history.

Examples / mini-scenarios:
- Move model X to eu-west1 only for prod: create binding with env=prod, region_preferences=[eu-west1], status=active. Router will see binding and only return clusters in eu-west1 for requests that match env=prod and have geo tag eu.
- Emergency failover: set binding.status=draining for primary cluster, router uses failover_order from policy to pick next candidate; traffic shifts automatically if health probes fail.

Open questions & decisions to make:
- ID scheme: UUIDs everywhere vs human-friendly slugs for teams/resources? Tradeoffs: slugs nice for UX but harder to guarantee immutability. Proposal: UUID PKs + optional aliases (slug) unique per owner_team.
- Does Binding need its own SLA profile, or inherit from Environment? Suggest inheritance but allow override for special dedicated customers.
- How expressive should RoutePolicy selectors be? Keep them limited (tag match + env) to avoid complexity.
- Cache TTL defaults: 5s for router-critical metadata vs 60s for non-critical. Need SLO discussion.

Next steps / action items:
- Review with router/scheduler (Arjun) to validate denormalized fields required by fast path.
- Product to decide on aliasing policy (Laura).
- Implement minimal CRUD prototype: Resources + Bindings + a tiny read cache. Outline of work in JIRA: JIRA-PLT-876 -> spike + PR.

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep control plane table schemas narrow: avoid huge JSON blobs. Prefer typed columns for common selectors.
- Event names should be stable: resource.binding.created, resource.binding.status_changed, cluster.registered.
- Consider a lightweight admin UI to let ops visualize binding-to-cluster mappings and do manual failovers.

References & links:
- internal: CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-1234 (routing performance notes)
- GH: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/402 (initial binding API sketch)
- Slack: #platform-ops thread pinned: "binding-drain-procedure"

Unresolved items for meeting:
- Cache invalidation guarantees between config writes and router read cache (strong vs eventual).
- Exact shape of cluster capability snapshot required by router.

End of working notes.
